title: Special Topics in Iberian and Latin American Studies; Speaking Up/Out: Women Writers and Feminist Social Movements in Contemporary Latin America
description:
Prerequisite: SPAN331, SPAN332, SPAN333, SPAN361, SPAN362, or SPAN363; or permission of instructor.

The feminist song "El violador eres tu" (The Rapist is You) - originally performed by the collective "Las Tesis" in Valparaiso, Chile - has become a global hymn to protest violence against women. The performance was based on the work of anthropologist Rita Segato, whose studies have exposed power structures and the systematic violations of womens rights. By reading contemporary women writers, and by working on contemporary feminist social movements, this course will explore what Segato has defined as "the war against women". Thus, this seminar will explore how feminist subversion of naturalized power relationships have become a social force that is reshaping Latin American culture in the last decades. Particularly, we will explore how contemporary cultural artifacts contest value systems while rejecting hierarchies and norms.
